question: Compare memory bandwidth of the Apple M4 Pro and M5 Pro.

message.content: The Apple M4 Pro chip has a maximum memory bandwidth of 273 GB/s [4]. In contrast, the Apple M5 Pro chip has a maximum memory bandwidth of 307 GB/s [3]. Therefore, the M5 Pro offers higher memory bandwidth than the M4 Pro.

passages.heading: Memory
passages.text:
### Memory

[edit]
The M4 is packaged with LPDDR5X unified memory, supporting 120GB/sec of memory bandwidth. The SoC is offered in 8GB, 12GB, 16GB, 24GB, and 32GB configurations, with the 8GB and 12GB configuration only being available on the iPad. <sup>[3]</sup>

The M4 Pro is available with up to 64GB unified memory (Mac Mini) with a theoretical maximum bandwidth of 273GB/sec.<sup>[12]</sup> The M4 Max is capable of addressing up to 128GB unified memory, with over half a terabyte per second (546GB/sec) of memory bandwidth, with a slightly reduced bandwidth (410GB/sec) for the binned 32-core M4 Max.<sup>[13]</sup>

passages.heading: Apple M5 Pro & M5 Max GPU Analysis - M5 Max GPU on par with the GeForce RTX 5070 and faster than Strix Halo
passages.text: The M5 Pro shifts Apple's core naming conventions and features an 18-core CPU setup. It combines **6 "Super Cores"** (10-Wide Architecture with up to 4.6 GHz) which deliver the world's fastest single-threaded performance via an enhanced cache hierarchy and increased front-end bandwidth—with **12 "Performance Cores"** (7-Wide Architecture with up to 4.4 GHz) optimized for power-efficient multithreaded processing. According to Apple, this new configuration results in up to a 30% increase in multithreaded performance for demanding pro workloads compared to the M4 Pro. The new P-Cores slot in between the E-Cores of the M5 (6-Wide Architecture with 3.05 GHz) and should offer around 70% of the performance of the Super cores according to this source.

passages.heading: Apple M5 Pro & M5 Max GPU Analysis - M5 Max GPU on par with the GeForce RTX 5070 and faster than Strix Halo
passages.text:
Additionally, the chip boasts a nice bump in AI performance. By integrating a faster **16-core Neural Engine** and placing dedicated Neural Accelerators inside each GPU core, the M5 Pro pushes over 4x the peak GPU compute for AI compared to its predecessor.

The M5 Pro supports up to **64 GB of unified memory** with a maximum memory bandwidth of **307 GB/s**. The SoC also packs Apple’s latest Media Engine (supporting hardware-accelerated H.264, HEVC, AV1 decoding, and ProRes encode/decode) and introduces native, on-chip controllers for **Thunderbolt 5**.

The SoC is manufactured in the modern 3nm process at TSMC (N3P).

passages.text:
# Apple M4

Benchmarks & Specs

                Last updated: 

            Benchmarks & Specs

With the Apple M4, Apple consolidates its lead in ARM-based desktop and mobile architecture. While the M3 made the jump to the 3 nm process (N3B), the M4 uses the refined second-generation 3 nm manufacturing (N3E). This not only allows higher clock speeds but above all a clearly improved energy efficiency under the same load.

passages.heading: Apple M4
passages.text:
The graphics unit has 10 cores and continues features such as hardware-accelerated ray tracing and mesh shading. For gamers and 3D designers in particular, this means realistic lighting calculated in real time, something that was previously unthinkable on an SoC of this size.

A key focus is the Neural Engine (NPU). With 16 cores it reaches a computing power of 38 TOPS (trillion operations per second). This makes the M4 well equipped for local AI workflows and Apple Intelligence.

The**Apple M4** uses LPDDR5X-7500 memory, which results in a bandwidth of 120 GB/s. This is a critical factor for GPU performance and AI workloads, as both benefit greatly from fast data throughput.

passages.heading: **Architecture and CPU Performance**
passages.text:
## **Architecture and CPU Performance**

The M5 Pro shifts Apple's core naming conventions and features an 18-core CPU setup. It combines **5 of the 6 "Super Cores"** (10-Wide Architecture with up to 4.6 GHz) which deliver the world's fastest single-threaded performance via an enhanced cache hierarchy and increased front-end bandwidth—with **10 of the 12 "Performance Cores"** (7-Wide Architecture with up to 4.4 GHz) optimized for power-efficient multithreaded processing. According to Apple, this new configuration results in up to a 30% increase in multithreaded performance for demanding pro workloads compared to the M4 Pro. The new P-Cores slot in between the E-Cores of the M5 (6-Wide Architecture with 3.05 GHz) and should offer around 70% of the performance of the Super cores according to this source.

passages.heading: **Architecture and CPU Performance**
passages.text:
Compared to other SoCs, the 15-core M5 Pro should be able similar to the older 16-core M4 Max, positioning itself at the top of the mobile SoC class. In terms of single-core performance, the M5 Pro should deliver comparable results to the Apple M5, which topped our charts in Geekbench 6.5 Single, for example (ahead of the Qualcomm Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme X2E-96-100 and the M4 SoCs).

For graphics, the SoC scales up to a next-generation **16-core GPU** (4 deactivated). It features an enhanced shader core, second-generation dynamic caching, and hardware-accelerated mesh shading. This delivers up to 20% higher raw graphics performance than the M4 Pro.

passages.heading: **Architecture and CPU Performance**
passages.text:
Additionally, the chip boasts a nice bump in AI performance. By integrating a faster **16-core Neural Engine** and placing dedicated Neural Accelerators inside each GPU core, the M5 Pro pushes over 4x the peak GPU compute for AI compared to its predecessor.

The M5 Pro supports up to **24 GB of unified memory** with a maximum memory bandwidth of **307 GB/s**. The SoC also packs Apple’s latest Media Engine (supporting hardware-accelerated H.264, HEVC, AV1 decoding, and ProRes encode/decode) and introduces native, on-chip controllers for **Thunderbolt 5**, allowing for unprecedented high-speed I/O connectivity.

The SoC is manufactured in the modern 3nm process at TSMC (N3P).
